en.greeting: Hi! Today you learn to join two ideas into one sentence with who, which, that and where, just like Indonesian 'yang'. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: One sentence, two ideas
steps.text: You already do this in Indonesian with 'yang'. Let's see how English does it.
steps.body: *I have a friend. She works in a bank.* → *I have a friend **who works in a bank**.* The part after *friend* is a **relative clause**: it tells us **which** person, thing or place you mean. Indonesian uses **yang** for everything; English chooses: **who** for people, **which** for things and animals, **that** for both, **where** for places. **who** takes the place of **she**, so don't keep both.

steps.title: People and things
steps.text: Read these out loud. Is it a person or a thing?
steps.body: For a person say **who** or **that**; for a thing **which** or **that**. Both are correct. **which** is never for people.

examples.en: I have a friend who works in a bank.
examples.id: Saya punya teman yang bekerja di bank.

examples.en: The girl that sits next to me is from Medan.
examples.id: Cewek yang duduk di sebelah saya berasal dari Medan. (that juga bisa untuk orang)

examples.en: This is the bus which goes to the airport.
examples.id: Ini bus yang ke bandara.

examples.en: Do you know a restaurant that sells good rendang?
examples.id: Kamu tahu restoran yang jual rendang enak?

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A person or a thing?

question.prompt: The woman ___ cuts my hair has opened her own salon in Bandung.
options: which
who
where
question.explanation: The woman is a **person**, so use **who** (that is also fine, but it isn't an option here). **which** is only for things and animals, and **where** is for places.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Your company is looking for a new driver. Join the idea into one sentence.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kami butuh sopir yang kenal Jakarta.
question.solution: We need a driver who knows Jakarta.
question.explanation: A driver is a person, so **who** comes right after *a driver*. **who** replaces *he/she*: *We need a driver. He knows Jakarta.* → *We need a driver who knows Jakarta.*

steps.title: Places: where or which?
steps.text: Indonesian often says 'tempat' for a place: kantor tempat saya bekerja. English has a special word.
steps.body: Use **where** + person + verb: *the office **where I work***. *'the office which I work'* is a common mistake. **Trick:** make the small sentence with **there**. *I work there* ✓ → **where**. If the place itself does something or is the thing you visit or like, there is no 'there': *the mall **which** opened last month*, *the city **which** I visited*. (*the office which I work in* is also correct, but **where** is shorter.)

pairs.id: kantor tempat saya bekerja (I work there)

pairs.en: the school where my kids study
the mall which opened last month
pairs.id: mal yang baru buka bulan lalu (mal itu yang buka)
kota yang saya kunjungi (I visited it)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Try the 'there' trick.

question.prompt: This is the hotel ___ we stayed during our holiday in Bali.
options: which
where
who
question.explanation: We stayed **there**, so use **where**. *'the hotel which we stayed'* is missing *in* at the end, and **who** is only for people.

steps.title: Don't say it twice
steps.text: Here's a mistake many learners make, even at B1.
steps.body: Normally *bought* needs a thing after it: *I bought **it***. But in *the book **that** I bought*, **that** already means *the book*, so the place after *bought* stays empty. Indonesian is the same: *buku yang saya beli*, not *'buku yang saya beli buku itu'*. So no **it / him / her / them**: *'the book that I bought it'* ✗.

steps.title: Spot the correct one
steps.text: Only one sentence is right. Look at what comes after bought.

options: The shoes that I bought them online are too small.
The shoes I bought them online are too small.
The shoes that I bought online are too small.
question.explanation: **that** already means *the shoes*, so nothing comes after *bought*: *The shoes that I bought online are too small.* The other two repeat the shoes with **them**.

steps.title: Keep it or drop it?
steps.text: In English you can often leave out who, which or that. Look at the word right after it.
steps.body: A **person or thing + verb** comes next (*we ordered, you sang*): the word is the **object** (the thing that receives the action) → you **can** leave it out. A **verb** comes next (*took, work*): the word is the **subject** (the one who does it) → it **must** stay.

examples.en: The food we ordered was cold.
examples.id: Makanan yang kami pesan dingin. (setelahnya 'we' → that boleh hilang)

examples.en: The song you sang at the party was great.
examples.id: Lagu yang kamu nyanyikan di pesta itu bagus sekali. (setelahnya 'you' → boleh hilang)

examples.en: The driver who took me home was very kind.
examples.id: Sopir yang mengantar saya pulang sangat baik. (setelahnya 'took' → who wajib)

examples.en: The people who work here are friendly.
examples.id: Orang-orang yang bekerja di sini ramah. (setelahnya 'work' → who wajib)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Look at the word after that in each sentence.

question.prompt: In which sentence can you leave out that?
options: The man that fixed my motorbike was very friendly.
The motorbike that I bought last year uses a lot of petrol.
The app that shows the KRL times is free.
question.explanation: In the motorbike sentence, **I** comes after that, so that is the object and can go: *The motorbike I bought last year…* In the other two, a verb (*fixed, shows*) comes next, so that must stay.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Relative clauses
artifact.intro: Which word to use after the noun, and when you can leave it out.
rows: the man who lives next door
the bus which goes to the airport
the girl that sits next to me
a place that does something or that you visit
the mall which opened last month
tips: Don't say it twice: the book that I bought (not 'bought it'), the man who lives here (not 'who he lives').
The 'there' test: I work there → the office where I work. No 'there' → which or that.
Never which for people, never what for 'yang'.

examples.en: I have a friend who works in a bank.
examples.id: Saya punya teman yang bekerja di bank.

examples.en: The email Rina sent was very long.
examples.id: Email yang dikirim Rina panjang sekali.

examples.en: That's the office where I work.
examples.id: Itu kantor tempat saya bekerja.

steps.text: Want more practice? These links explain the same ideas in other words.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar menggabungkan dua ide jadi satu kalimat dengan who, which, that dan where, persis seperti 'yang' dalam bahasa Indonesia. Yuk, kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Satu kalimat, dua ide
steps.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu sudah melakukannya dengan 'yang'. Yuk lihat caranya dalam bahasa Inggris.
steps.body: *I have a friend. She works in a bank.* → *I have a friend **who works in a bank**.* Bagian setelah *friend* disebut **relative clause**: bagian 'yang …' yang menjelaskan orang, benda atau tempat **yang mana** yang kamu maksud. Bahasa Indonesia memakai **yang** untuk semuanya; bahasa Inggris memilih: **who** untuk orang, **which** untuk benda dan hewan, **that** untuk keduanya, **where** untuk tempat. **who** menggantikan **she**, jadi jangan pakai keduanya.

steps.title: Orang dan benda
steps.text: Baca dengan suara keras. Orang atau benda?
steps.body: Untuk orang pakai **who** atau **that**; untuk benda **which** atau **that**. Keduanya benar. **which** tidak pernah dipakai untuk orang.

examples.en: I have a friend who works in a bank.
examples.id: Saya punya teman yang bekerja di bank.

examples.en: The girl that sits next to me is from Medan.
examples.id: Cewek yang duduk di sebelah saya berasal dari Medan. (that juga bisa untuk orang)

examples.en: This is the bus which goes to the airport.
examples.id: Ini bus yang ke bandara.

examples.en: Do you know a restaurant that sells good rendang?
examples.id: Kamu tahu restoran yang jual rendang enak?

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Orang atau benda?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: The woman ___ cuts my hair has opened her own salon in Bandung.
options: which
who
where
question.explanation: The woman adalah **orang**, jadi pakai **who** (that juga benar, tapi tidak ada di pilihan). **which** hanya untuk benda dan hewan, dan **where** untuk tempat.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Kantormu sedang mencari sopir baru. Gabungkan idenya jadi satu kalimat.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kami butuh sopir yang kenal Jakarta.
question.solution: We need a driver who knows Jakarta.
question.explanation: Sopir adalah orang, jadi **who** datang tepat setelah *a driver*. **who** menggantikan *he/she*: *We need a driver. He knows Jakarta.* → *We need a driver who knows Jakarta.*

steps.title: Tempat: where atau which?
steps.text: Untuk tempat, bahasa Indonesia sering bilang 'tempat': kantor tempat saya bekerja. Bahasa Inggris punya kata khusus.
steps.body: Pakai **where** + orang + kata kerja: *the office **where I work***. *'the office which I work'* adalah kesalahan yang sering terjadi. **Trik:** buat kalimat kecilnya dengan **there** (di sana). *I work there* ✓ → **where**. Kalau tempat itu sendiri yang melakukan sesuatu, atau tempat itu yang kamu kunjungi atau sukai, tidak ada 'there': *the mall **which** opened last month*, *the city **which** I visited*. (*the office which I work in* juga benar, tapi **where** lebih pendek.)

pairs.id: kantor tempat saya bekerja (I work there)

pairs.en: the school where my kids study
the mall which opened last month
pairs.id: mal yang baru buka bulan lalu (mal itu yang buka)
kota yang saya kunjungi (I visited it)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Coba trik 'there'.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: This is the hotel ___ we stayed during our holiday in Bali.
options: which
where
who
question.explanation: Kami menginap **di sana** (we stayed there), jadi pakai **where**. *'the hotel which we stayed'* kurang kata *in* di akhir, dan **who** hanya untuk orang.

steps.title: Jangan disebut dua kali
steps.text: Ini kesalahan yang sering dibuat, bahkan di level B1.
steps.body: Biasanya *bought* butuh benda setelahnya: *I bought **it***. Tapi di *the book **that** I bought*, **that** sudah berarti *the book*, jadi tempat setelah *bought* dibiarkan kosong. Bahasa Indonesia juga begitu: *buku yang saya beli*, bukan *'buku yang saya beli buku itu'*. Jadi jangan tambahkan **it / him / her / them**: *'the book that I bought it'* ✗.

steps.title: Mana yang benar?
steps.text: Hanya satu kalimat yang benar. Lihat apa yang ada setelah bought.

options: The shoes that I bought them online are too small.
The shoes I bought them online are too small.
The shoes that I bought online are too small.
question.explanation: **that** sudah berarti *the shoes*, jadi tidak ada apa-apa setelah *bought*: *The shoes that I bought online are too small.* Dua kalimat lainnya mengulang sepatunya dengan **them**.

steps.title: Dipakai atau dihilangkan?
steps.text: Dalam bahasa Inggris, who, which atau that sering boleh dihilangkan. Lihat kata tepat setelahnya.
steps.body: Kalau setelahnya ada **orang atau benda + kata kerja** (*we ordered, you sang*): kata itu adalah **objek** (yang dikenai pekerjaan) → **boleh** dihilangkan. Kalau setelahnya langsung **kata kerja** (*took, work*): kata itu adalah **subjek** (pelakunya) → **wajib** ada.

examples.en: The food we ordered was cold.
examples.id: Makanan yang kami pesan dingin. (setelahnya 'we' → that boleh hilang)

examples.en: The song you sang at the party was great.
examples.id: Lagu yang kamu nyanyikan di pesta itu bagus sekali. (setelahnya 'you' → boleh hilang)

examples.en: The driver who took me home was very kind.
examples.id: Sopir yang mengantar saya pulang sangat baik. (setelahnya 'took' → who wajib)

examples.en: The people who work here are friendly.
examples.id: Orang-orang yang bekerja di sini ramah. (setelahnya 'work' → who wajib)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Lihat kata setelah that di tiap kalimat.

question.prompt: Di kalimat mana kamu boleh menghilangkan that?
options: The man that fixed my motorbike was very friendly.
The motorbike that I bought last year uses a lot of petrol.
The app that shows the KRL times is free.
question.explanation: Di kalimat motor, setelah that ada **I**, jadi that adalah objek dan boleh hilang: *The motorbike I bought last year…* Di dua kalimat lainnya, setelahnya langsung kata kerja (*fixed, shows*), jadi that wajib ada.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman.

Tes 'there': I work there → the office where I work. Tidak ada 'there' → which atau that.
which tidak pernah untuk orang, dan what tidak pernah dipakai untuk 'yang'.
